review_notes: Preflight NEEDS_REVIEW (interface-vs-method judgement, no auto-signals). Resolved by cold read: the instruction and submission_format.md state the interface only (two files, header, allowed labels, five keys); layout_spec.md states the domain rules (page size, running order, length, floor, verdict priority, figure meanings) and never a method or tool. Guess points listed and each settled in the text: line numbering from 1 ('the first passage beginning on the first line'); which page a passage is on ('the page its first line falls on'); several decisions on one edit (About sheet: 'An edit's latest decision is its call.'); what a decision means (About sheet: accepted / deferred / withdrawn, and 'A decision that returns an edit to an earlier call makes the edit stand as that call did.'; each of the 15 wordings has one reading, declared in derive_gold.py DECISIONS and listed in README section 4); several edits on one passage ('every accepted edit proposed for it'); a cut to exactly zero ('never falls below 1 line'); whether the held line moves later passages ('The lines the floor holds back are real lines'); verdict precedence ('whatever else is true of it'); final page ('the page the manuscript's last line falls on'); row order ('in any order'); id form ('PS-04, not PS4 or 4'). The requester leads ('nothing has been struck from it'; 'Tomas's Not in sheet lists every edit that isn't going into this pass') are literally true: no line was deleted, and derive_gold.py asserts the Not in sheet lists exactly the edits whose call is not accepted. Neither says whether an edit not going in is deferred or withdrawn; the About sheet does.

review_notes: Preflight NEEDS_REVIEW x3. (a) domain_correctness, 'are the domain figures fictional or exactly cited?': fictional and self-contained. The manuscript, passages, line counts and edits are invented; the 30-lines-a-page layout is the fixture's own spec, stated in layout_spec.md, not a claim about any real press or style guide; the instruction cites nothing. No figure needs an external source. (b) workflow_realism, 'would a professional recognise this ask?': yes. After a copyedit or second read, an author or production editor re-derives page references for flagged or queried passages (index entries, cross-references, permissions and proof queries), accepted and deferred changes are tracked-change states, and a passage whose text is cut away keeps its place-holding line (scene break or heading) so later pages do not jump. An edit register kept as a running log of decisions in the readers' own words across two reads, with calls revisited (a cut restored pending the author, a parked addition accepted, a line count revised), is how editorial queries are tracked in practice; two independent edits proposed against the same draft passage that together exceed it are routine when two readers mark the same draft. (c) Leakage, as mined: the instruction named the deciding case and its remedy ('One of the cuts is as long as the passage it is cutting, so do not let that passage vanish and pull everything else back with it'), and the ledger's edit_code column did the passage-edit join for the agent.
change_made: Floor hint removed from the instruction; the join moved into the data (register kept as a dated log in a workbook, keyed by edit_code, with a passage_id column; ledger carries no edit code); decisions recorded in the readers' own words, as real query logs are, with an About sheet and a reader's not-in list. Nothing from solution/ or tests/ reaches the image.
